obligations.summary: The Commission shall annually assess the need to amend the list in Annex III and the prohibited AI practices in Article 5, and submit its findings to the European Parliament and the Council.

By 2 August 2028 and every four years thereafter, the Commission shall evaluate and report to the European Parliament and Council on the need for amendments to Annex III, Article 50 transparency measures, and the supervision and governance system.

By 2 August 2029 and every four years thereafter, the Commission shall submit a public evaluation and review report on this Regulation to the European Parliament and Council, including an assessment of enforcement structure and the possible need for a Union agency.
Reports under paragraph 2 shall pay specific attention to national competent authority resources, Member State penalties, harmonised standards, and the number of SMEs entering the market.
By 2 August 2028, the Commission shall evaluate the functioning, powers, and competences of the AI Office and submit a report thereon to the European Parliament and Council.

By 2 August 2028 and every four years thereafter, the Commission shall submit a public report to the European Parliament and Council reviewing progress on standardisation for energy-efficient development of general-purpose AI models and assessing the need for further measures.

By 2 August 2028 and every three years thereafter, the Commission shall evaluate the impact and effectiveness of voluntary codes of conduct for non-high-risk AI systems, including environmental sustainability considerations.

The Board, Member States, and national competent authorities shall provide the Commission with information upon request and without undue delay for the purposes of carrying out evaluations and reviews under paragraphs 1 to 7.
In carrying out evaluations and reviews, the Commission shall take into account the positions and findings of the Board, the European Parliament, the Council, and other relevant bodies or sources.

The Commission shall, if necessary, submit appropriate proposals to amend this Regulation, taking into account technological developments, effects on health, safety, and fundamental rights, and the state of progress in the information society.
The AI Office shall develop an objective and participative methodology to guide evaluations of risk levels and the inclusion of new systems in the lists under Annex III, Article 5, and Article 50.

Any amendment to this Regulation or related acts concerning sectoral Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I Section B shall take into account the regulatory specificities of each sector and existing governance and enforcement mechanisms.

By 2 August 2031, the Commission shall carry out an assessment of the enforcement of this Regulation and report to the European Parliament, the Council, and the European Economic and Social Committee, accompanied where appropriate by a proposal for amendment.
